What it measures: Size + effort from operator/operand counts
Key formula/basis: V = N·log2(n); E = D·V
Evidence note (primary source): Derived constants never re-validated; survives mostly inside composite indices (MI). Halstead 1977
Strengths: Language-agnostic, cheap, no parser needed beyond tokens
Limitations: Ignores control flow and structure entirely; effort/bug estimates unsupported
Agent-loop use: Weak. Use only as a size proxy inside composites

What it measures: Independent paths through the control-flow graph
Key formula/basis: V(G) = E − N + 2P
Evidence note (primary source): Landman et al. 2016 (17.6M Java methods, 6.3M C functions): CC correlates with SLOC but NOT strongly enough to be redundant
Strengths: Simple, universal, maps to minimum test-path count
Limitations: Weights all decisions equally; ignores nesting; correlates heavily with size at aggregate level
Agent-loop use: Good gate at function level; useless as a repo-level average

What it measures: Effort to intuitively understand code
Key formula/basis: +1 per flow break, extra weight per nesting level
Evidence note (primary source): Muñoz Barón, Wyrich & Wagner, ESEM 2020: meta-study over 427 snippets / ~24k human ratings — correlates with comprehension TIME and subjective ratings; mixed for correctness and physiological measures
Strengths: Only code-only metric with published human-comprehension validation
Limitations: Heuristic, language-tuned; validated for time-to-understand, not for defects
Agent-loop use: Strong. The closest proxy to 'will a human or model struggle here'

What it measures: Composite ease of maintenance
Evidence note (primary source): van Deursen 2014 'Think Twice Before Using the Maintainability Index': opaque constants, unreproducible calibration, size dominates the formula
Strengths: Single executive-friendly 0–100 number
Limitations: Composite hides its own driver; effectively a size metric in disguise; not reproducible across tools
Agent-loop use: Avoid as an agent target — it is the most gameable number on this list

What it measures: Raw or logical volume
Key formula/basis: Line and statement counts
Evidence tier: A — strongest single predictor, but a confound
Evidence note (primary source): Sjøberg et al. TSE 2013: after adjusting for file size, NONE of 12 code smells predicted maintenance effort; only size and low cohesion did
Strengths: Trivially computable; dominates most other metrics statistically
Limitations: Almost every 'sophisticated' metric is partly re-measuring size — always control for it
Agent-loop use: Essential as a CONTROL variable, not as a quality target

What it measures: Interdependency and internal relatedness
Key formula/basis: CBO, RFC, LCOM, WMC, DIT
Evidence tier: B — validated for OO defect proneness
Evidence note (primary source): CK 1994 + replications; LCOM/cohesion is one of the two survivors in Sjøberg 2013
Strengths: Captures design structure, not just line counts
Limitations: Requires OO structure; LCOM has ~6 incompatible definitions across tools
Agent-loop use: Useful for 'where should this be split' guidance

What it measures: Hierarchy depth, class surface area
Key formula/basis: DIT, NOM counts
Evidence note (primary source): Inconsistent results across replications; narrow applicability
Strengths: Flags pathological hierarchies
Limitations: Narrow; near-useless outside deep OO codebases
Agent-loop use: Low priority

What it measures: Copy-paste and near-clone volume
Key formula/basis: Token- or AST-level clone detection; % duplicated lines
Evidence tier: B — validated, and the key AI-era signal
Evidence note (primary source): GitClear 2026 (623M changes, 2023–2026): +81% code-block duplication, +41% within-commit copy/paste, cross-file reuse −35%, refactoring line-moves −70% vs 2022
Strengths: Hard to fake; directly measures the failure mode AI assistants actually cause
Limitations: Clone detection thresholds are tunable and vendor-specific
Agent-loop use: HIGH. This is the metric that catches an agent solving by copy-paste

What it measures: Change frequency, churn, code age, ownership diffusion, bus factor
Key formula/basis: Commit counts, added/deleted lines over time windows, author entropy
Evidence note (primary source): Rahman & Devanbu ICSE 2013 'How, and why, process metrics are better' + Majumder et al., EMSE 2021 large-scale replication: process metrics beat product metrics for within- and cross-project defect prediction; product metrics are too static to discriminate
Strengths: Predictive, cheap (git only), language-agnostic
Limitations: Needs history — useless on a fresh file or a new repo
Agent-loop use: HIGH, and structurally ungameable by an agent editing a single file

What it measures: Complexity weighted by change frequency; files that change together
Key formula/basis: Hotspot = churn × complexity; temporal coupling = co-commit frequency
Evidence tier: B — the basis of CodeScene's commercial model
Evidence note (primary source): Tornhill, 'Your Code as a Crime Scene'; change coupling correlates with defect proneness
Strengths: Prioritizes effort where it pays; surfaces hidden architectural coupling no static tool sees
Limitations: Sensitive to history window and to repo-wide refactors/reformats
Agent-loop use: HIGH. Answers 'is this a risky place to change' — the question agents never ask

What it measures: Cycles, coupling direction, modularity
Key formula/basis: Afferent/efferent coupling (Ca/Ce), instability I = Ce/(Ca+Ce), abstractness, distance from main sequence, dependency cycles, propagation cost (DSM transitive closure)
Evidence note (primary source): MacCormack et al. 2006 (propagation cost / DSM); architectural-smell studies link cycles, God components and dense structure to higher bug-fix LOC share
Strengths: Catches the damage that per-file metrics structurally cannot see
Limitations: Expensive to compute; needs real symbol resolution, not regex
Agent-loop use: HIGH for agents — blast radius is exactly what a local edit cannot perceive

What it measures: Does the suite actually detect faults
Key formula/basis: Mutation score = mutants killed / mutants generated
Evidence note (primary source): Just et al. FSE 2014 (Defects4J, 5 OSS projects, ~230k mutants): 73% of real faults were coupled to generated mutants. Inozemtseva & Holmes ICSE 2014 (31k suites): coverage is only weakly correlated with effectiveness once suite size is controlled — 'should not be used as a quality target'
Strengths: Mutation is the only test metric with fault-detection validity
Limitations: Expensive (minutes to hours); language-specific tooling
Agent-loop use: HIGH-VALUE, HIGH-COST. The single best defense against an agent writing assertion-free tests

What it measures: Which lines executed under test
Key formula/basis: Executed lines / total; diff coverage on changed lines only
Evidence tier: C — weak as a target, useful as a gap-finder
Evidence note (primary source): Inozemtseva & Holmes 2014 (above)
Strengths: Cheap, universal, diff-scoped version is genuinely actionable
Limitations: Trivially gamed — the classic assertion-free test passes 100% coverage
Agent-loop use: Use as a NEGATIVE signal only (uncovered new code), never as a score

What it measures: Predicted human readability from surface + textual features
Key formula/basis: Buse & Weimer 2010 (25 syntactic features); Scalabrino et al. JSEP 2018 (104 features incl. textual/identifier quality)
Evidence note (primary source): Scalabrino 2018: +6.2% accuracy over structural-only models by adding textual features
Strengths: Directly models the human judgment, not a proxy for it
Limitations: Trained on small Java corpora; generalization across languages is unestablished
Agent-loop use: Medium. Identifier/naming quality is the transferable part

What it measures: Whether THIS change made things better or worse
Key formula/basis: Delta Maintainability Model: classify changed lines low/high risk, score = low-risk proportion (di Biase et al., TechDebt 2019; implemented in PyDriller)
Evidence note (primary source): DMM extends the SIG model (Heitlager et al. QUATIC 2007) from snapshots to commits
Strengths: The only formulation that fits a per-commit agent loop; immune to inherited legacy debt
Limitations: Coarse (binary risk bucketing); SIG thresholds are proprietary in origin
Agent-loop use: HIGHEST fit for an agent loop — absolute scores punish agents for pre-existing debt

What it measures: Counted violations of a defined weakness catalog
Key formula/basis: ISO/IEC 5055:2021 (CISQ): security, reliability, performance-efficiency, maintainability weaknesses; CWE-mapped
Evidence note (primary source): ISO/IEC 5055:2021 — first ISO standard measuring quality from internal structure; CWE severity is expert consensus, not measured impact
Strengths: Auditable, defensible, vendor-neutral, contract-usable
Limitations: Counts ≠ risk; severity weighting is judgment, not evidence
Agent-loop use: Good for the 'hard gate' tier — deterministic and explainable

What it measures: Remediation effort as money or time
Key formula/basis: Debt ratio = remediation effort ÷ estimated redevelopment effort (Letouzey 2009)
Evidence note (primary source): Sonar's default '10 min per excess unit of cognitive complexity' is an assumption, not time-tracked data
Strengths: Communicates to non-engineers; comparable over time within one tool
Limitations: Fake precision — dollar figures inherit made-up per-rule remediation times
Agent-loop use: Report the components, never the dollar figure, to an agent

What it measures: Vulnerable, typosquatted, hallucinated, or unmaintained dependencies
Key formula/basis: CVE/OSV matching, OpenSSF Scorecard checks, package-existence verification
Evidence note (primary source): SonarQube 2026.4 shipped supply-chain gate conditions specifically for agents pulling typosquatted or hallucinated packages
Strengths: Real, exploitable outcomes rather than proxies
Limitations: Not a 'quality' signal — a distinct risk axis; noisy without reachability analysis
Agent-loop use: MANDATORY for agent loops — package hallucination is an agent-specific failure mode

What it measures: Throughput and stability of delivery
Key formula/basis: Lead time, deploy frequency, change failure rate, failed-deployment recovery time
Evidence note (primary source): DORA 2025: AI adoption raises throughput ~2–18% while stability declines; change failure rates rise without strong automated testing and fast feedback
Strengths: Measures what the business actually feels
Limitations: Lagging; team-level, not attributable to a file or a commit
Agent-loop use: Ground truth for CALIBRATING the code-level metrics — not a per-edit signal

What it measures: Realized defects per unit of code
Key formula/basis: Defects per KLOC; incident linkage to commits
Evidence note (primary source): Standard in defect-prediction literature; the thing other metrics are validated AGAINST
Strengths: Unarguable
Limitations: Lagging by weeks to months; requires linked issue/incident data
Agent-loop use: The label to train and validate everything else against

What it measures: How expensive this code is for an AI agent to work in
Key formula/basis: Context bytes needed to comprehend a change; retrieval locality (files touched per task); test feedback latency; blast radius (transitive dependents)
Evidence note (primary source): Adjacent evidence only: CodeScene/Borg 2026 — higher code health raises agent refactoring test-pass rates and smell removal (52% vs 5.7% with guidance); 'Not All Code Is Equal' (2026) — complexity degrades LLM reasoning
Strengths: Measures the actual bottleneck in an agentic pipeline; genuinely unclaimed territory
Limitations: No validation, no baselines, no prior art to lean on — you would be defining it
Agent-loop use: The defensible original axis, if you validate it rather than assert it

What it measures: Whether the score improved because the CODE improved
Key formula/basis: Suppression-comment density (noqa/eslint-disable), deleted or skipped tests, coverage-exclusion drift, assertion-free tests, threshold edits in config, lookup-table blowups
Evidence note (primary source): SpecBench 2026: 90th-percentile reward-hacking gap grows ~27pp per 10x LOC; one agent wrote a 2,900-line lookup table to hit 97% validation with 0% held-out. Static-analysis feedback loop study (2025): iterative refinement fixed most issues but INTRODUCED new vulnerabilities in ~5% of iterations
Strengths: Directly counters the failure mode created by putting a metric in an agent's loop
Limitations: Adversarial arms race; false positives on legitimate suppressions
Agent-loop use: The feature no incumbent will build, because it makes their own score look uncertain
